lines: A Karplus-Strong delay line tuned to pitch, with up to seven unison voices on every polyphonic channel
Tunes the delay time in whole octaves, -4 to +4, added to whatever V/OCT carries
Tunes the delay time in semitones, -7 to +7, added to whatever V/OCT carries
Sets how much of the delayed signal returns to the delay line, 0 to 50%
Sets the number of unison voices on each polyphonic channel, 1 to 7
Sets how far the unison voices are detuned from one another
Sets the level of the detuned unison voices against the centre voice
Lengthens the ring by feeding the delay line back at full level on a random proportion of samples
Sets the delay time as a pitch, 1V per octave, 0V giving C4 at 261.63Hz
Added to the FEEDBACK knob, 10V for the whole range
The signal written into the delay line; its channel count sets the polyphony
Added to the COUNT knob, one unison voice per volt
Added to the SPREAD knob, 10V for the whole range, and a negative voltage acts as its own magnitude
Added to the MIX knob, 10V for the whole range, and a negative voltage acts as its own magnitude
Added to the STRETCH knob, 10V for the whole range
The unison mix read out of the delay line, limited and with DC removed
KSDelay.notes: Parameter 7, Stretch Lock, has no widget on the panel; the line creating it is commented out in the source, so it is left untagged.

lines: An emulation of a ladder filter in six modes, with a resonance that will self-oscillate

Attenuverts the frequency modulation input, -1 to +1
Attenuverts the resonance input, -1 to +1
Sets the resonance, 0 to 10, self-oscillating towards the top of the range
Attenuverts the drive input, -1 to +1
Sets the drive into the filter, 0 to 2
Selects the mode: LP12, LP24, HP12, HP24, BP12 or BP24
Shifts the cutoff frequency, 1V per octave, added to the FREQUENCY knob
Modulates the resonance through its attenuverter, 5V at full attenuverter covering the whole range
Modulates the drive through its attenuverter, 5V at full attenuverter covering the whole range
The audio into the filter; its channel count sets the polyphony
Modulates the cutoff frequency through its attenuverter, 1V per octave at full attenuverter
The filtered audio
Note — with nothing patched to the audio input the filter keeps running, and at high resonance it works as a sine oscillator tracking V/OCT
Maccomo.notes: The README says the six modes are selectable by CV as well as by the knob, and the code does read a mode CV input, but no jack for it was ever placed on the panel; input 3 is therefore unreachable and untagged.

Shifts the cutoff frequency, 1V per octave, added to the FREQUENCY knob

Amburgh.notes: Input 3 is a mode CV input with no jack on the panel, and unlike Maccomo the code does not read it; it is left untagged.

lines: A feedforward comb filter with a feedback loop, which makes pitched sound out of noise and adds overtones to sound that is already pitched
Sets the frequency of the harmonic bands, -4 to +4 octaves from C4 at 261.63Hz
Attenuverts the frequency modulation input, -1 to +1
Attenuverts the comb input, -1 to +1
Sets the magnitude of the harmonic bands, -1 to +1; positive values boost them and negative values cut them
Attenuverts the feedback input, -1 to +1
Sets how much of the delayed signal returns to the delay line; the result is clamped at 0.9 either way
Shifts the frequency of the harmonic bands, 1V per octave, added to the FREQUENCY knob
Modulates the band frequency through its attenuverter, 1V per octave at full attenuverter
Modulates the comb amount through its attenuverter, 5V at full attenuverter covering the whole range
Modulates the feedback through its attenuverter, 5V at full attenuverter covering the whole range
The audio into the comb filter; its channel count sets the polyphony
The comb filtered audio, limited and with DC removed
A shift register with a monophonic input and a polyphonic output: each trigger samples the input and moves the stored voltages along one channel
Sets how many polyphonic channels the register fills, 1 to 16
Sets the chance that an incoming trigger is skipped, 0 to 1
Sets the chance that the stored voltages are reordered when a trigger arrives, 0 to 1
Sets the chance that the Accent A offset is added to a stored voltage, 0 to 1
Sets the voltage Accent A adds, -10V to +10V
Sets the chance that the Accent B offset is added to a stored voltage, 0 to 1
Sets the voltage Accent B adds, -10V to +10V
Sets the chance that a random accent is added to a stored voltage, 0 to 1
Sets the largest voltage the random accent can add, -10V to +10V; the amount used each time is a random fraction of it
Added to the CHANNELS knob, one channel per volt
Added to the TRIGGER PROBABILITY knob, 10V for the whole range; a polyphonic cable here lets every channel skip independently
Added to the SHUFFLE PROBABILITY knob, 10V for the whole range; a polyphonic cable here lets every channel reorder independently
Added to the ACCENT A PROBABILITY knob, 10V for the whole range; a polyphonic cable here gives every channel its own chance
Added to the ACCENT A OFFSET knob, volt for volt
Added to the ACCENT B PROBABILITY knob, 10V for the whole range; a polyphonic cable here gives every channel its own chance
Added to the ACCENT B OFFSET knob, volt for volt
Added to the ACCENT RNG PROBABILITY knob, 10V for the whole range; a polyphonic cable here gives every channel its own chance
Added to the RNG MAX OFFSET knob, volt for volt
The voltage sampled into the register on each trigger
A rising edge drops the channel count back to one, and it climbs again by one on every trigger
A rising edge samples the input and moves the stored voltages along one channel
The stored voltages with their accent offsets added, one per polyphonic channel
PolyShiftRegister.notes: The IN jack and the OUT jack carry whatever is patched in, most often pitch but not always, so neither is given a family. The reset and trigger jacks are the last two inputs by index and are not in panel order: input 11 is the TRIGGER jack and input 10 the RESET jack.

lines: An expander for Tyrant, placed immediately to its right, which turns Tyrant's probability decisions into polyphonic triggers
A trigger on each channel whose incoming clock pulse was skipped
A trigger on each channel whose stored voltages were reordered
A trigger on each channel that received the Accent A offset
A trigger on each channel that received the Accent B offset
A trigger on each channel that received the random accent
A trigger on every channel when Tyrant is reset

Sets the crossover frequency, marked in Hz, from 10Hz upwards
Attenuverts the frequency modulation input, -1 to +1
Modulates the crossover frequency through its attenuverter, 1V per octave at full attenuverter
The audio to be split; its channel count sets the polyphony
The band above the crossover frequency
The band below the crossover frequency
Note — the two bands sum back to a flat frequency response, so several of these can be chained to make any number of bands
A two way crossover that splits a stereo pair into low and high bands with fourth order Linkwitz-Riley filters
Sets the crossover frequency, marked in Hz, from 10Hz upwards
Attenuverts the frequency modulation input, -1 to +1
Modulates the crossover frequency through its attenuverter, 1V per octave at full attenuverter
The left channel to be split; its channel count sets the polyphony of the left outputs
The right channel to be split; its channel count sets the polyphony of the right outputs
The part of the left channel above the crossover frequency
The part of the right channel above the crossover frequency
The part of the left channel below the crossover frequency
The part of the right channel below the crossover frequency
Note — the two bands of a channel sum back to a flat frequency response, so several of these can be chained to make any number of bands
A slimline mixer that sums eight polyphonic inputs through a single attenuverter
One of the inputs into the sum, taken at unity gain
One of the inputs into the sum, taken at unity gain, despite Rack's tooltip for it reading Attenuverter
Sets the level of the summed inputs, -1 to +1, inverting the sum below zero
Added to the attenuverter, 5V for a change of one, and the total is clamped to -1 and +1
The summed inputs after the attenuverter, saturated near 10V, with the channel count of whichever input has the most channels
Eva.notes: The eight summing inputs and the output carry audio or CV depending on what is patched, so they are given no family. The maker's configInput call for the first input passes the output enum by mistake, so Rack shows that jack's tooltip as Attenuverter; the panel prints IN over the column.

lines: A performance controller that fades a parameter on another module between two values along an easing curve, either once on a trigger or cycling without stopping
Attenuverts the easing input, -1 to +1
Selects the easing curve: back, bounce, circ, cubic, elastic, expo, linear, quad, quart, quint or sine
Attenuverts the start value input, -1 to +1
Sets one end of the fade, -1 to +1 across the assigned parameter's range
Attenuverts the end value input, -1 to +1
Sets the other end of the fade, -1 to +1 across the assigned parameter's range
Attenuverts the duration input, -1 to +1
Sets the time taken to move from one end of the fade to the other, 0 to 2 times the clock period, and 0 to 2 seconds with nothing patched to SYNC
Selects cycling, where the value runs from one end of the fade to the other and back without stopping, or one shot, where a trigger at TRIG runs it once
Does by hand what a pulse at the SYNC input does, timing the clock period from one press to the next
Does by hand what a pulse at the TRIG input does, starting a one shot fade
Does by hand what a pulse at the PAUSE input does, stopping the fade and letting it continue
Shifts the easing curve through its attenuverter, added to the EASING SHAPE knob
Modulates the start value through its attenuverter, 5V at full attenuverter covering the whole range
Modulates the end value through its attenuverter, 5V at full attenuverter covering the whole range
Modulates the duration through its attenuverter, 5V at full attenuverter covering the whole range
A trigger stops the fade where it stands, and the next one lets it continue
A clock; the time between two pulses is the period the DURATION knob multiplies
In one shot mode a positive trigger runs the fade from the start value to the end value, and a negative-going trigger runs it back
The value being sent to the assigned parameter, -10V to +10V
Menu — Retrigger mode chooses what a trigger arriving mid-fade does: Restart begins the fade again, Ignore lets it finish
Menu — Duration Multiplier scales the DURATION knob by 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 50, 100, 500 or 1000
Note — click the parameter display and then click a knob on another module to assign it, and right-click the display to unassign it
A MIDI input for 14 bit continuous controllers, pairing each of CC 0 to 31 with the CC 32 numbers higher to give finer resolution than 128 steps
The value of its own pair of CC numbers, 0-10V, or -5V to +5V when the menu is set away from unipolar
Menu — the pairing mode sets how the two CC messages are combined: Midi 1.0, No Zeroing No Waiting, MSB LSB pair, and one in which the MSB is held back until its LSB arrives
Menu — the smoothing slider sets the time constant of the filter on every output, up to 67ms, and 33ms by default
Menu — Unipolar switches every output between 0-10V and -5V to +5V
Note — the display selects the MIDI device the module takes its messages from
Zilah.notes: The three parameters are reached only from the context menu and have no widget on the panel, so they are untagged.

lines: A trigger sequencer with eight tracks and four pages of sixteen steps, made to be played from a MIDI grid controller
Turns that step of its track on or off; while LENGTH, EUCLIDEAN or ROTATE is armed the press sets that instead
Turns that track on or off; a track that is off sends nothing to either of its outputs
Shows that quarter of the sequence on the grid, without interrupting any track
Sets every track back to its first step
Advances every track by one step
Arms the grid so that the next step pressed becomes the last step of that track, which is what lets tracks run at different lengths
Arms MIDI learn, so that a control moved on the MIDI controller and a control then clicked here are mapped to one another
At one the main output of that track follows the programmed steps exactly; below one it is the chance that a programmed step plays, and above one it adds a chance that an unprogrammed step plays
Sets the chance that a step of that track which is not programmed plays on the alt output
Arms the grid so that the next step pressed sets the number of hits spread evenly across that track's length
Arms the grid so that pressing the first step of a track rotates its pattern one step left, and pressing the second step rotates it one step right
A rising edge advances every track by one step, and the voltage present here is what the outputs pass on, so the output pulses keep the width of the clock
A rising edge sets every track back to its first step
Passes the clock pulse through whenever the programmed step on that track plays
Passes the clock pulse through on steps of that track which are not programmed, for ghost hits and alternating voices
Menu — Probability Notch Width adds a flat zone in the middle of the main probability controls, so an imprecise fader gives exactly the programmed pattern
Menu — Clear Midi Mapping and Clear all Midi Mappings drop the mappings made by MIDI learn
Menu — Midi Learn Parameter First reverses the order of MIDI learn, so a control here is clicked before the controller is moved
Menu — Use Rotary Encoders reads the probability controls as endless encoders rather than as absolute faders
Menu — Slow midi feedback thins out the messages sent back to the controller
Menu — factory MIDI mappings are provided for the APC Mini, the Launchpad Mk2 and Mk3 and the APC Key 25
Note — a grid controller lights up only once both its MIDI input and its MIDI output are assigned, and two controllers can be used, one for each half of the sixteen steps
Iverson.notes: Parameters 136 to 143 hold the per-track loop lengths and 168 to 175 the MIDI mapping settings; none of them has a widget on the panel, so they are untagged.

lines: A small FM oscillator with feedback, usable as a VCO or an LFO, every instance carrying its own slight detune and its own noise floor
Multiplies the frequency by two raised to its setting, -4 to +4, for dialling an FM ratio
Raises the pitch in whole semitones, 0 to 12
Shifts the pitch in whole octaves, -5 to +5
Sets how far the FM input moves the phase, 0 to 1
Sets how much of the output is folded back into its own phase, which adds harmonics to the sine
Sets the pitch, 1V per octave; its channel count sets the polyphony
Attenuates the FM input, 10V passing it at the depth the DEPTH knob sets and 0V removing it
Attenuates the feedback, 10V passing the amount the FEEDBACK knob sets and 0V removing it
The signal that modulates the phase, plus or minus 5V for the full depth
The oscillator, plus or minus 5V before the scale and offset in the menu
Menu — Default Tuning sets what 0V at V/OCT means: Audio C4 at 261.63Hz, Clock or LFO at 2Hz, or Slow LFO at 0.125Hz
Menu — Unison trades polyphony for detuned copies of the voice, 1 to 16, summed down to one channel
